Classroom & Skill-Lab Teaching

Classroom teaching methods, micro-teaching, and skill laboratory practice in nursing education.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Use classroom teaching methods appropriately
  • Describe micro-teaching
  • Plan a skill laboratory session
  • Give effective explanation and demonstration

In simple words

Good teaching matches the method to the lesson: large groups get lectures, but skills need demonstration and practice, and problems need discussion.

Classroom methods

Method When best Watch out
Lecture New information to a large group Becomes passive; keep it short
Discussion Attitudes and application Needs preparation
Brainstorming Many ideas quickly No judgement
Role play Sensitive situations and empathy Debrief afterwards
Case study Decision making Needs prior knowledge
Team teaching Combining expertise Needs planning
Computer assisted learning Self-paced revision Needs facilities
Project Independent learning Needs clear goals

Micro-teaching

A short teaching session (5-10 minutes) with a small group, focused on one skill, followed by feedback.

  1. Plan one specific skill
  2. Teach for 5-10 minutes with peers observing
  3. Feedback — strengths, areas to improve
  4. Reteach the same skill after changes
  5. Teachers repeat until the skill improves

Skill laboratory practice

  1. Prepare — objectives, station, equipment, checklist
  2. Demonstrate — the teacher performs the skill step by step, with commentary
  3. Guided practice — students practise with supervision
  4. Return demonstration — each student performs back
  5. Evaluation — record against a checklist; extra practice until safe

Rules of demonstration: speak audibly, face the group, go slowly through critical steps, avoid turning your back, and repeat the critical step.

🔴 Return demonstration is compulsory

A student who has only watched cannot perform safely. Every student must give a return demonstration before clinical practice.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Choose the method to match the learning objective.
  2. Micro-teaching: plan, teach, feedback, reteach.
  3. Demonstration steps: prepare, demonstrate, practise, return demo, evaluate.
  4. Keep the group facing you; narrate critical steps.
  5. Skill lab practice must precede patient contact.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Lecture is passive; mix with questions and examples.
  2. Role play needs a debrief to convert experience into learning.
  3. Brainstorming generates ideas; evaluation comes later.
  4. Team teaching needs preparation and shared planning.
  5. Record students against checklists for fairness.

📌 Memory trick

Skill lab: D-P-R-E — Demonstrate, Practise, Return demonstration, Evaluate.

60-second revision

  • Match method to aim: lecture, discussion, role play, project.
  • Micro-teaching: plan, teach, feedback, reteach.
  • Skill lab: demonstrate, practise, return demonstration, evaluate.
  • Demonstration rules: audible, visible, slow critical steps.
  • Return demonstration before patient care.

Test yourself

Micro-teaching is a session of:

Answer: B. Micro-teaching is a very short teaching session focused on a single skill, followed by feedback and reteaching.

Before contacting a patient, a nursing student must:

Answer: B. Return demonstration in the skill lab ensures the student can perform safely before patient contact.

Which method best develops empathy?

Answer: B. Role play allows students to experience another person’s situation and develop empathy.

During demonstration, the teacher should:

Answer: A. The teacher must face the group, be visible, narrate critical steps and avoid hiding the hands.

Brainstorming is used to:

Answer: B. Brainstorming produces many ideas rapidly; evaluation and ranking happen afterwards.
